sender: Grant Halloran, Director of Institutional Sales, Silverline CareData
subject: Senior housing occupancy hit 88.6% in Q3 - see which operators are pulling ahead (sample + demo)
body:
Hi Ellen,

Senior housing has quietly become one of the cleaner demand stories in healthcare real estate, and we wanted to put numbers on it before the REIT earnings season starts.

From the Silverline CareData Q3 release (covering 14,800 communities, about 1.1m units):
- Stabilized occupancy: 88.6% (+90bp q/q, +310bp y/y)
- Independent living: 90.2%; assisted living: 87.1%; memory care: 85.4%
- Net absorption: ~9,400 units in the quarter, the strongest Q3 since we began tracking in 2018
- New supply: starts remain at ~1.3% of inventory annualized, versus a 20-year average near 3%
- Rate growth on in-place residents: +5.8% average; move-in rates up 4.1%

Why it matters: Occupancy is now within ~400bp of the pre-2020 peak. With starts constrained by construction costs and financing, we believe the sector is heading into a multi-year period of rate-driven NOI growth. Operators with high exposure to the Sunbelt and to assisted living look best positioned in our scoring model. Our top-decile operator list is in the sample file.
